result:
My final answer, adaptive LIRS, is in `final.py`. It scores **0.5716** on the search split, against 0.365 for the LRU baseline. I used **13 of the 24 scorer calls** and about 14 of the default 15 minutes.

| | Search score (official) | Held-out (my own harness, unseen seeds) |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (LRU) | 0.365 | 0.348 |
| First champion (W-TinyLFU) | 0.503 | 0.425 |
| W-TinyLFU with ghost-steered window | 0.544 | 0.485 |
| **Final (adaptive LIRS)** | **0.5716** | **0.510** |

The scorer only covers the search split, so the held-out column comes from my own trace generator on seeds I never tuned on. It ranks the four in the same order as the scorer.

**Why it beats LRU:** it is LIRS, which keeps keys whose reuse gaps are short and stable. That holds steady when a loop is larger than the cache (shifting_loops goes from about 0 to 0.83) and when one-off scans pass through. Plain LIRS was weaker on recency traces (0.77 against LRU's ~0.85). So I made the share of the cache given to newcomers adaptive:
- **It grows** when a recently evicted newcomer comes back after a short gap, meaning a little more room would have caught it.
- **It shrinks** faster when an evicted key that had been one of the long-term keepers comes back.

That raised recency to 0.815 without losing the loop gains. I also made one change for unseen traces: trimming LIRS's history list now runs only now and then instead of copying the list on every miss. A 100k-key scan takes 0.06 s, and a full scorer run takes about 1 s against the 8 s limit.

**Families tried (official search score):** LRU 0.365, ARC 0.407, S3-FIFO 0.443, W-TinyLFU 0.503, W-TinyLFU with hill-climbed window 0.479, W-TinyLFU with ghost-steered window 0.471 → 0.544 after fixes, plain LIRS 0.566, adaptive LIRS 0.5716.

**How the search went:**
- My first harness ranked candidates in the wrong order. I rebuilt it as six trace types matching the trace names the scorer prints (hot_with_scans, loop_and_hot, phases, mixed, recency, shifting_loops), using only my own reading of those names. After that its rankings matched the scorer's.
- Two ideas were tested on the harness only and dropped: picking the lowest-frequency victim from several old entries, and different protected-segment sizes.
- The last round of constant tuning (gate, step size, history-list bound) was flat within noise, so I stopped there.

The two weakest traces, hot_with_scans and mixed, sit around 0.24–0.26 for every policy I tried. On my harness they are about 0.07–0.09 below the offline optimum, so little is left to gain there. All files are in the `cache/` folder: `harness.py` and `gen2.py` are the local harness, and the scorer logged each call in `calls.log`.
